newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends up, but well off highs.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends up, but well off highs.

text.p: COMEX copper futures ended up Friday, but well off the session's highs, though the short term outlook remained bullish, analysts said.

"This market remains largely technical in nature, although exchange stock levels and news of supply disruptions have proven price supportive on a short-term basis over the past few weeks," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.
"Near term momentum could take prices back to the 96 cents resistance, but profit taking would likely then spark another sell off."
COMEX December copper ended up 0.80 cent at 91.25 cents, but well of the intraday highs at 93.40 cents.
The whole copper strip surged higher early in line with LME copper, after a further fall in LME stocks.
LME copper stocks fell 9,300 tonnes to 247,325 tonnes Friday, and have fallen 18,125 tonnes this week, with further declines seen likely in the weeks ahead as consumption rises.
But COMEX copper stocks rose 287 short tons to 21,819 short tons Thursday.
The December/March backwardation ended slightly wider at 1.10 cents.
LME three month copper saw a four week high at $1990 early Friday, with the LME October options expiry next Wednesday was seen as a short term bullish factor also.
The fallout from the Sumitomo affair, which rocked the copper market mid-year also now appears to be over, while the prompt market remains firm, traders said.
